messages:
alice: heads up — two prod inference hosts hit OOM around 03:12 UTC during a ~10k token convo. kv_cache usage shot up and the hosts couldn't reclaim fast enough. logs: https://ops/logs/incident/2180009123 :thinking_face:

maria: thanks, saw the alert. perf-bot telemetry shows a ~3.2x increase in kv_cache.bytes_active vs baseline right before OOM. memory growth looks steady during long-polls, not a single spike.

ben: is this the long-context customer we've been testing with? if so their request pattern keeps appending, so prefix reuse is high but we might be keeping too many sticky entries.

zach: quick triage — can you paste the stack snippet? I want to see if kernel selection is switching to the quantized kernel that uses a different KV layout.

alice: stack excerpt: ````
runtime: kv_cache::allocate_entry(size=1.2GB)
...
kv_cache::mark_sticky(entry=0x7f8a)
allocation failed: out of memory
````
(not the full dump, linked above)

perf-bot: alert: kv_cache.active_growth_rate > 95th_pct for 4m. hosts where OOMed: infer-rt-14, infer-rt-19. Related metric: kv_cache.fragmentation_ratio up 0.22.

sara: two immediate mitigations to consider: 1) temporary per-host cap on kv cache growth, 2) trigger anchored-eviction experiment for long-context sessions. anchored-eviction = preferentially evict older prefixes from the same session to prevent single convo from owning the pool.

ben: agree. also we should look at batching heuristics — if we switch some legacy customers to smaller batch windows their KV reuse drops and we free space. but that's a perf vs cost trade.

maria: proposal for quick canary (manual steps):
1) deploy runtime config change to set kv_cache.max_growth_ratio=0.15
2) enable kv_cache.eviction.mode=anchored for canary hosts infer-rt-19,infer-rt-21
3) add a short TTL to sticky prefixes: kv_cache.sticky_ttl_seconds=900
4) enable spill-to-disk softbackoff: kv_cache.spill.enabled=true (disabled by default)

zach: +1 to canary. what's the exact flag for anchored eviction?

maria: it's `kv_cache.eviction.strategy=anchored_v1` (experimental). quick patch:
```
# runtime config snippet
kv_cache:
  eviction:
    strategy: anchored_v1
    anchored_threshold: 0.6   # fraction of pool owned by one session before anchor kicks in
  max_growth_ratio: 0.15
  sticky_ttl_seconds: 900
  spill:
    enabled: true
    max_disk_bytes: 10GB
```

alice: if we enable spill-to-disk we need to measure latency tail — disk access will increase p99. can we do a soft fallback where we degrade to model-variant (smaller kv footprint) for the session that triggered growth?

ben: yes, we have routing policy `fallback:model-small` that can be triggered by runtime when kv_cache.owner_share > 0.5. we can wire that into anchored_v1 to auto-fallback after 1 retry.

perf-bot: suggestion: collect these telemetry points before/after canary: kv_cache.owner_share, fragmentation_ratio, active_bytes, spill_reads, per-request p50/p95/p99 latency. tag by session_id.

sara: long-term fixes we should track:
- smarter reuse heuristics that collapse similar prefixes (dedupe keys for repeated prefixes)
- periodic compaction worker that coalesces adjacent small slabs to reduce fragmentation
- kernel selection guard: avoid quant-kernel paths that increase slab-fragmentation for longctx workloads

zach: on the kernel note, we saw last quarter that switching to the vectorized attention kernel reduced token latency but increased transient allocs for KV intermediate buffers. that could be contributing under long contexts. logging added: `runtime.kernel.last_switched=vector_attn_v2` around the incidents. we should add an opt-out for longctx sessions.

alice: ok action items for this thread (short-term):
- maria: push canary config to infer-rt-19/21 (anchored_v1 + max_growth_ratio + sticky_ttl + spill enabled) — target: next 10m
- ben: add auto-fallback hook to anchored_v1 to route to `model-small` after 1 failed allocation — target: EOD
- zach: add kernel opt-out for session length > 4k tokens in runtime selector — target: 24h
- sara: build dashboard widget with metrics from perf-bot for the canary hosts — target: 1h

maria: deploying canary now, will post rollout link.

deploy-bot: deploy started by maria to cluster infer-rt-canary (hosts: infer-rt-19, infer-rt-21). change: kv_cache.eviction.strategy=anchored_v1. track at https://deploys/2180009123

perf-bot: baseline snapshot captured at T0. will report deltas after 15m.

alice: if canary looks good let's also add a small playbook note under eng-runtime/playbooks/kv-oom.md: short blurb + rollback steps (set eviction.strategy=default, disable spill). I'll draft after we verify metrics.

ben: one more paranoid mitigation: attach a hard oom-killer hook that will gracefully reject new longctx growth requests (HTTP 429 with reason=kv_capacity) to avoid host crash. low-impact and preserves other sessions.

sara: agreed. I'll add 429 path to the runtime with a metric kv_rejections.count so product can be routed.

alice: thanks all. keep updates in this thread. ping me if you see a canary OOM. :thumbsup:
